basis: Facts from research/niches/social.json (every number has its source and checked date). Crowd scores are our judgment from the playbook table, before real member data.

crowd.note: Thin margins and high churn. Lead with one clear result a month. Pitch 4 to 6 weeks before their big dates (judgment).
not_yet: Don't sell 30 posts a month first. Start with one week they can see.
Don't buy a camera. A phone and good window light are enough.
Don't chase chains. Owner-run spots decide in one visit.

starter_kit.item: Scheduling: the restaurant's free Meta Business Suite, or Buffer or Metricool free plans

sources.says: Free plan for 3 channels with 10 scheduled posts per channel; Essentials $5 a month per channel; Team $10 a month per channel.
Starter $18.75 a month billed yearly (1 social set, 30 posts per profile); Growth $37.50 a month billed yearly.
Free $0 for 1 brand and 20 posts a month; Starter from $20 a month billed yearly or $25 month to month.
Doing it yourself with Meta Business Suite costs nothing but the manager's time; a scheduler costs $0 to about $25 a month.
Social media companies: general liability $33 a month, BOP $56 a month, media liability $78 a month (median of Insureon quotes).
Marketing consultants: general liability $30 a month ($357 a year); professional liability $59 a month.

job_checklist: Before you start: signed one-page agreement, first month paid, one goal for the month (for example, fill Tuesday nights) and how you will count it together.
Access: the owner adds you as a partner in Meta Business Suite and as a manager on their Google Business Profile. Never ask for passwords.
Facts sheet: menu with prices as printed, hours, specials, the owner's voice, words to avoid, allergy notes, what not to show.
Plan the month: 3 posts and 1 Reel a week, a Google profile post every week, dates that matter to them.
Shoot day: 60 to 90 minutes before service in window light, dish by dish, plus hands, prep, staff who agreed, the room and the sign.
Write captions: what it is, the price as printed, when to come, how to order or book; 3 to 5 hashtags.
Owner approval: one sheet with every post; nothing goes out without a yes.
Schedule in Meta Business Suite or the scheduler; reply to comments on the days you agreed.
Month end: a one-page report with counts you both can see (posts made, reach and saves from Insights, the goal count the owner kept) and next month's plan.

objections.says: We tried social media and it didn't bring anyone in.
objections.answer: Pick one goal for one month (for example, a slow night) and count it together with the owner; no promise of results, only of the posts on time.

objections.says: My nephew or a server does our Instagram.
objections.answer: Offer a shoot day and a month of planned posts they can keep running, or help on weeks they are busy.
Start smaller: one week of posts or one shoot. Restaurants run on thin margins, so the first package stays small.

objections.says: Our regulars know us. We don't need it.
objections.answer: New guests find places by word of mouth and walking by first, then Facebook and Instagram; posts give regulars something to share.

objections.says: I don't want to give someone my password.
objections.answer: You never need it: partner access lets them choose exactly what you can touch and remove it any time.

licenses.check: City or county business license, state registration if you form an LLC, and a DBA if you use a name other than your own.

sources.says: Licenses and permits depend on business activity and location; research your own state, county and city.

licenses.check: Free from the IRS; handy for a business bank account.

sources.says: Get an EIN directly from the IRS in minutes for free.

licenses.item: Who owns the photos and videos you make
licenses.check: You own what you shoot unless a signed written agreement says otherwise. Put the usage you grant (their social accounts, website, menus) in the proposal, and keep the right to show the work in your portfolio.

sources.says: A commissioned work is a work made for hire only in certain categories and only if the parties expressly agree in a written instrument signed by them.

licenses.item: Disclose any free meals or pay on your own posts
licenses.check: If you post about a client on your own account, or get a free meal to feature a place, say so plainly in the post itself.

sources.says: Disclose the relationship if you got anything of value to mention a product, such as free or discounted products or services; place the disclosure with the endorsement; don't use vague terms like sp, spon or collab.

licenses.check: Business accounts get Meta's Sound Collection, not the popular songs catalog. Use Sound Collection tracks or the restaurant's own sound.

sources.says: The Meta Sound Collection is available to every account type including business accounts, cleared for Facebook and Instagram only; a business account sees the Sound Collection instead of the licensed catalog.

licenses.check: Ads that show or invite people to drink must target 21 and older in the US and follow local law; check your state's rules on drink specials.

sources.says: Ads promoting alcohol must comply with local laws and target people 21 and older in the United States; an invitation to an alcohol venue counts.

licenses.check: Ask staff and guests before they appear in a post; keep it to staff who agreed.

licenses_note: General information, not legal advice. Rules differ by state, county and city: check your state and city before you take paid jobs.

where_buyers_look.channel: In person: owners decide at the counter, between the lunch and dinner rush

sources.says: 66% of respondents said the top source of referrals for new business is their existing and past clients; referrals from partner companies were second at nearly 13%.

where_buyers_look.channel: Their own guests' habits (why owners care)

sources.publisher: Toast (survey of 1,446 US adults, Oct 9 to 15, 2025)
sources.says: Word of mouth is the top discovery channel at 38%, then walking or driving past at 30%; Facebook 27%, Instagram 15%, YouTube 15%, TikTok 14%; TikTok is the top discovery channel for Gen Z at 38%.

sources.publisher: Restaurant Dive, citing Toast's 2019 Restaurant Success Report
sources.says: 91% of restaurants use Facebook; Instagram use rose from 24% to 78% in a year.

steps: List 25 owner-run restaurants and cafes near you (Your first 25).
Make a sample week for the best one from their own menu and photos as found: 3 post graphics in their colors, captions, and one Reel shot list.
Walk in between lunch and dinner with it on your phone, or send it with a short note; follow up on day 3 and day 7.
Never post it or present it as their account; it's a sample they can say yes to.
Write down 10 spots where you're a regular.
Ask the owner for 10 minutes and show the sample week.
Offer the founding price for the first 3 in exchange for an honest testimonial you may quote.

plays.play: Partners who see owners every week
steps: List suppliers, POS and delivery reps, a local food blogger, the chamber of commerce.
Show them one sample week and your one clear package.
Ask who could use help; thank them with a referral gift that isn't tied to any review.
Offer a founding price to your first 3 in exchange for an honest testimonial you may quote and permission to show the work.
Say plainly that they were founding clients.
Never tie a Google review to the discount.

rules.rule: Up to 5 hashtags on an Instagram post or Reel
rules.detail: Instagram is moving every account to a 5 hashtag cap per caption. Write 3 to 5 that say what and where.

rules.rule: Reels can run up to 3 minutes; the profile grid is now tall, not square
rules.detail: Make feed posts 1080 by 1350 (4:5) and keep the words in the middle so the tall grid crop doesn't cut them.

rules.rule: Business accounts use the Sound Collection for music
rules.detail: Popular songs may not be available to a restaurant's business account; plan Reels around original sound or Sound Collection tracks.

rules.rule: Get access as a partner, not with their password
rules.detail: The owner adds you as a partner in their Meta business portfolio (Settings, Business settings, Partners, Add) and picks which pages and accounts you can use.

rules.rule: No buying followers, views or reviews
rules.detail: Never buy followers or views for a client and never write reviews. Growth is reported as counted, not promised.
A restaurant can ask every guest for a review but can't offer a discount, a dessert or anything else for one, and can't ask only happy guests.
Post updates and offers on the restaurant's Google profile too; use the Call now button instead of typing a phone number in the post.
3 to 5 feed posts or Reels a week is the common advice; 1 or 2 a week is the floor; Google profile at least once a week.

promise: Every post goes to you for a yes before it goes out, and it goes out on the day we agreed. If a post isn't right, I redo it free.

ladder.ask: an honest written testimonial I can quote, said plainly as a founding client, and permission to show the posts in my portfolio
ladder.step_up: After the first 3 months the plan goes to the full price, and after 3 founding clients new clients pay the full menu price.
ladder.reviews_rule: Ask for Google reviews separately, never tied to the discount (Google Maps content policy).
